chapters.title: The Beginning of the Good News
chapters.html:
Mark 1

John the Baptizer

1The beginning of the good news of Jesus the Messiah.

2As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "I am sending My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way;

3a voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.'"

4John the baptizer appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

5The whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

6John wore clothing of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.

7He preached, saying, "After me comes one who is stronger than I; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of His sandals.

8I have baptized you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

The Baptism and the Testing of Jesus

9In those days Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

10At once, as He was coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens torn open and the Spirit coming down on Him like a dove.

11A voice came from the heavens: "You are My Son, the beloved; in You I am well pleased."

12At once the Spirit drove Him out into the wilderness.

13He was in the wilderness forty days, being tested by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels served Him.

The First Disciples

14After John was handed over, Jesus went into Galilee, preaching the good news of God

15and saying, "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news."

16As He passed along beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew, Simon's brother, casting a net in the sea, for they were fishermen.

17Jesus said to them, "Come, follow Me, and I will make you become fishers of people."

18At once they left their nets and followed Him.

19Going on a little farther, He saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were in the boat mending the nets.

20At once He called them; and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and went after Him.

A Day in Capernaum

21They went into Capernaum, and at once, on the sabbath, He went into the synagogue and taught.

22They were astonished at His teaching, for He was teaching them as one who has authority, and not as the scribes.

23At once, there in their synagogue, was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,

24"What have You to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are: the Holy One of God."

25Jesus rebuked him, saying, "Be silent, and come out of him!"

26The unclean spirit threw him into convulsions, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.

27They were all amazed, so that they asked one another, "What is this? A new teaching, with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him."

28At once the report of Him went out everywhere, into all the surrounding region of Galilee.

29At once they left the synagogue and went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

30Simon's mother-in-law was lying in bed with a fever, and at once they told Him about her.

31He came to her, took her by the hand and raised her up; the fever left her, and she began to serve them.

32When evening came, after the sun had set, they brought to Him all who were ill and those possessed by demons.

33The whole town was gathered at the door.

34He healed many who were ill with various diseases, and drove out many demons; and He would not let the demons speak, because they knew Him.

35Very early in the morning, while it was still dark, He got up and went out to a deserted place, and there He prayed.

36Simon and those with him hunted for Him,

37found Him, and said to Him, "Everyone is looking for You."

38He said to them, "Let us go elsewhere, into the nearby towns, so that I may preach there also; for that is why I came out."

39He went preaching in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and driving out the demons.

A Leper Made Clean

40A leper came to Him, pleading with Him on his knees and saying to Him, "If You are willing, You can make me clean."

41Moved with anger, He stretched out His hand and touched him, and said to him, "I am willing; be made clean."

42At once the leprosy left him, and he was made clean.

43He sternly warned him and at once sent him away,

44saying to him, "See that you say nothing to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

45But he went out and began to proclaim it freely and to spread the word, so that Jesus could no longer go openly into a town, but stayed out in deserted places; and people came to Him from everywhere.

Notes

  • v1 "The beginning of the good news of Jesus the Messiah" — archē, beginning, is the first word of Genesis in Greek, en archē. Euangelion, good news, is the word for a herald's message, as in Isaiah's herald of good news (Isaiah 40:9) and How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news (Isaiah 52:7). The edition marks Messiah as a place where manuscripts differ.

  • vv2–3 "As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: I am sending My messenger before Your face" — the first lines are not Isaiah's but Exodus 23:20, I am sending a messenger before you, joined to Malachi 3:1, I am sending My messenger, and he will clear the way before Me, as in Matthew 11:10. Only v3 is Isaiah 40:3. Mark names the greater prophet for all three. The edition marks in Isaiah the prophet as a place where manuscripts differ.

  • vv4–6 "John the baptizer… camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist… locusts and wild honey" — ho baptizōn, the baptizer, the one who baptizes. Baptisma metanoias, a baptism of repentance: metanoia is a change of mind, a turning back. John is dressed as Elijah was, a hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist (2 Kings 1:8), the prophet promised before the day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5). Locusts are clean food, the locust of every kind (Leviticus 11:22).

  • vv10–11 "the heavens torn open… You are My Son, the beloved; in You I am well pleased" — schizomenous, torn open, as Isaiah prayed, Oh, that You would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1); Mark uses the same verb at the end for the curtain of the sanctuary (15:38). The voice joins You are My son (Psalm 2:7) and My chosen one, in whom My soul delights (Isaiah 42:1). Ho agapētos, the beloved, is the Greek word for Isaac, your beloved one (Genesis 22:2). In Matthew the voice says This is My Son (Matthew 3:17); in Mark it speaks to Jesus.

  • vv12–13 "the Spirit drove Him out… forty days… with the wild animals, and the angels served Him" — ekballei, drove out, the verb Mark uses for driving out demons (1:34, 39). Forty days, as Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights (Exodus 34:28). Only Mark has the wild animals.

  • vv14–15 "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news" — kairos, the time, the appointed time, not the passing of hours. Ēngiken, has come near, the word of Matthew 3:2 and 4:17; Mark says the kingdom of God where Matthew says the kingdom of heaven.

  • vv16–20 "fishers of people… they left their father Zebedee in the boat" — Jeremiah's fishers were sent to gather the people for judgment, I am about to send for many fishers… and they will fish for them (Jeremiah 16:16). Elisha asked first to kiss his father and mother (1 Kings 19:20); these men leave at once.

  • vv21–28 "as one who has authority, and not as the scribes… What have You to do with us… the Holy One of God" — exousia, authority, the word that runs through the chapter (vv22, 27) and into 2:10. Ti hēmin kai soi, What have You to do with us, word for word What to us and to You?, as the widow said to Elijah, What have I to do with you, man of God? (1 Kings 17:18). Phimōthēti, Be silent, word for word Be muzzled. In v31 ēgeiren, raised her up, is the verb later used of Jesus rising (16:6), and she began to serve, diēkonei, as the angels did (v13).

  • vv40–42 "A leper came to Him… Moved with anger, He stretched out His hand and touched him" — lepros, leper: the law's tsara'at (Leviticus 13:45–46), the person who must live outside the camp and cry Unclean! Jesus touches him. Orgistheis, moved with anger, is the edition's reading, and it marks the word as a place where manuscripts differ; at what Jesus is angry, the verse does not say.

  • vv43–45 "show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded" — the law of the blight's cleansing, He shall be brought to the priest (Leviticus 14:2). Embrimēsamenos, sternly warned, a word for snorting with anger. The man spreads the word anyway, and Jesus, who was free to enter towns, now must stay outside them, like the leper before Him.

chapters.title: Lord Even of the Sabbath
chapters.html:
Mark 2

A Paralyzed Man Forgiven and Healed

1When He came back to Capernaum after some days, it was heard that He was at home.

2Many gathered, so that there was no longer room for them, not even at the door; and He was speaking the word to them.

3Some people came, bringing to Him a paralyzed man, carried by four of them.

4When they could not bring him to Him because of the crowd, they removed the roof above where He was; and when they had dug through, they let down the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.

5When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralyzed man, "Child, your sins are forgiven."

6Some of the scribes were sitting there, reasoning in their hearts,

7"Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?"

8At once Jesus, knowing in His spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves, said to them, "Why are you reasoning about these things in your hearts?

9Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up, pick up your mat, and walk'?

10But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — He said to the paralyzed man,

11"I say to you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home."

12He got up, at once picked up the mat, and went out in front of them all, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this!"

The Call of Levi

13He went out again beside the sea; all the crowd came to Him, and He taught them.

14As He passed by, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and He said to him, "Follow Me." He got up and followed Him.

15As He was reclining at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and His disciples; for there were many of them, and they followed Him.

16When the scribes of the Pharisees saw that He was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, they said to His disciples, "Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?"

17When Jesus heard it, He said to them, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but those who are ill. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."

The Bridegroom

18John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. People came and said to Him, "Why do John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Your disciples do not fast?"

19Jesus said to them, "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

20But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast, on that day.

21No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and the tear becomes worse.

22No one pours new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and the skins as well. New wine goes into fresh wineskins."

Lord of the Sabbath

23One sabbath He was going through the grainfields, and as they made their way His disciples began to pick the heads of grain.

24The Pharisees said to Him, "Why are they doing what is not lawful on the sabbath?"

25He said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him —

26how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the Presence, which it is not lawful for anyone but the priests to eat, and gave some also to those who were with him?"

27He said to them, "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.

28So the Son of Man is Lord even of the sabbath."

Notes

  • vv3–4 "carried by four of them… they removed the roof… let down the mat" — apestegasan tēn stegēn, they unroofed the roof, and exoryxantes, dug through. Krabattos, mat, a poor man's bedding; Matthew has klinē, bed (Matthew 9:2).

  • vv5–7 "Child, your sins are forgiven… Who can forgive sins but God alone?" — aphientai, are forgiven, said without naming who forgives. The scribes hear the LORD's own word, I, I am He who blots out your transgressions (Isaiah 43:25), and heis ho theos, God alone, word for word one, God, is the creed, the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4).

  • vv8–12 "knowing in His spirit… the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — tō pneumati autou, in His spirit, Jesus' own spirit, lowercase. Ho huios tou anthrōpou, the Son of Man, Jesus' name for Himself, from Daniel's vision, there came one like a son of man (Daniel 7:13), to whom authority was given. The visible healing is the proof of the forgiveness no one can see. The sentence breaks off as He turns to the man.

  • vv14–15 "Levi the son of Alphaeus… reclining at table in his house" — Matthew names him Matthew (Matthew 9:9). Telōnion, the tax booth, where tolls were taken. In his house: Levi's, or Jesus' own (2:1, at home); the Greek does not make it plain. Katakeisthai, reclining, the posture at a feast.

  • vv18–20 "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?… taken away from them" — hoi huioi tou nymphōnos, word for word the sons of the bridal chamber, the groom's friends. The prophets call the LORD Israel's bridegroom, as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God will rejoice over you (Isaiah 62:5). Aparthē, is taken away, is found only here and in the same saying in Matthew and Luke: the first hint of His death.

  • vv21–22 "a patch of unshrunk cloth… new wine into old wineskins" — agnaphou, unshrunk, not yet washed by the fuller; it shrinks and tears the old cloth. Kainos, new, and palaios, old, run through both sayings.

  • vv23–26 "pick the heads of grain… in the time of Abiathar the high priest… the bread of the Presence" — the law allowed picking by hand in a neighbor's field, you may pick the heads with your hand (Deuteronomy 23:25); the Pharisees object to doing it on the sabbath. In 1 Samuel the priest who gave David the bread is Ahimelech the priest (1 Samuel 21:1), Abiathar's father; epi Abiathar may mean in the time of Abiathar, or at the passage about Abiathar, as Mark names a passage of Exodus epi tou batou, at the passage about the bush (12:26). Hoi artoi tēs protheseōs, the bread of the Presence, set on the table… before Me always (Exodus 25:30), was given to David as holy bread (1 Samuel 21:6).

  • vv27–28 "The sabbath was made for man… the Son of Man is Lord even of the sabbath" — only Mark has v27. The sabbath was given as rest for all, you, or your son, or your daughter, your male slave… or your animal (Exodus 20:10). Anthrōpos, man, and the Son of Man are one word: the sabbath was made for man, and the Son of Man is its Lord.

chapters.title: Who Is My Mother?
chapters.html:
Mark 3

A Withered Hand on the Sabbath

1He went into the synagogue again, and a man was there whose hand was withered.

2They watched Him closely to see whether He would heal him on the sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.

3He said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and stand in the middle."

4Then He said to them, "Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?" But they were silent.

5He looked around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.

6The Pharisees went out and at once began plotting with the Herodians against Him, how they might destroy Him.

Crowds by the Sea

7Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judea,

8from Jerusalem, from Idumea, from beyond the Jordan, and from around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all that He was doing, came to Him.

9He told His disciples to have a small boat ready for Him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush Him;

10for He had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing on Him to touch Him.

11Whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, "You are the Son of God!"

12He sternly ordered them not to make Him known.

The Twelve

13He went up the mountain and called to Him those He wanted, and they came to Him.

14He appointed twelve, so that they might be with Him and that He might send them out to preach

15and to have authority to drive out the demons.

16He appointed the twelve: Simon, to whom He gave the name Peter;

17James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, to whom He gave the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder;

18Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean,

19and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over.

Beelzebul

20He went home, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.

21When His own people heard it, they went out to seize Him, for they were saying, "He is out of His mind."

22The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the ruler of the demons He drives out the demons."

23He called them to Him and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?

24If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

25If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

26If Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but his end has come.

27No one can enter the strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first ties up the strong man; then he will plunder his house.

28Truly I tell you, all things will be forgiven the sons of men, their sins and whatever blasphemies they utter;

29but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin" —

30for they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."

His Mother and His Brothers

31His mother and His brothers came, and standing outside they sent to Him and called Him.

32A crowd was sitting around Him, and they said to Him, "Your mother and Your brothers are outside, looking for You."

33He answered them, "Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?"

34Looking around at those who sat in a circle around Him, He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers!

35Whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother."

Notes

  • vv1–6 "to save a life or to kill?… with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts… with the Herodians" — psychēn sōsai, to save a life: the question turns from healing to killing, and in v6 the ones who watched Him plot to kill Him on the sabbath. Met' orgēs, with anger, as in 1:41. Pōrōsis, hardness, of skin grown callous; and the same root is used of the disciples' hearts (6:52). Hoi Hērōdianoi, the Herodians, supporters of Herod's house, named here first.

  • vv7–12 "Idumea… Tyre and Sidon… You are the Son of God!" — Idumea is the Greek name for Edom; the crowds come from every side of the land. The unclean spirits say what the voice from heaven said (1:11), and are silenced as in 1:34.

  • vv13–19 "He appointed twelve… Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder… Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over" — epoiēsen, appointed, word for word made. Mark gives the meaning of Boanerges. Simon the Cananaean, as Matthew 10:4. Paredōken, handed over, the word used of John in 1:14.

  • vv20–21 "His own people… went out to seize Him… He is out of His mind" — hoi par' autou, His own people, His family, who arrive in v31. Exestē, He is out of His mind, word for word He stands outside himself. The psalmist says, I have become a stranger to my brothers (Psalm 69:8). Mark sets the scribes' charge (vv22–30) inside the family's coming (vv21, 31–35).

  • vv22–27 "He has Beelzebul… How can Satan drive out Satan?… ties up the strong man" — Beelzeboul, as Matthew 12:24. Jesus is the stronger one John promised, ho ischyroteros (1:7), and binds ton ischyron, the strong man; Isaiah asks, Can the prey be taken from the mighty? (Isaiah 49:24).

  • vv28–30 "whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit… guilty of an eternal sin… He has an unclean spirit" — Amēn legō hymin, Truly I tell you, the first time in Mark. Tois huiois tōn anthrōpōn, the sons of men, all people. v30 says why the saying is given: they called the Holy Spirit in Him an unclean spirit.

  • vv31–35 "standing outside… those who sat in a circle around Him… Whoever does the will of God" — exō, outside, twice (vv31–32): the family stands outside, those who listen sit around Him. Matthew has the will of My Father in heaven (Matthew 12:50).

speech.text: Mark 3
A Withered Hand on the Sabbath
He went into the synagogue again, and a man was there whose hand was withered.
They watched Him closely to see whether He would heal him on the sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.
He said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and stand in the middle."
Then He said to them, "Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?" But they were silent.
He looked around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
The Pharisees went out and at once began plotting with the Herodians against Him, how they might destroy Him.
Crowds by the Sea
Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judea,
from Jerusalem, from Idumea, from beyond the Jordan, and from around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all that He was doing, came to Him.
He told His disciples to have a small boat ready for Him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush Him;
for He had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing on Him to touch Him.
Whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, "You are the Son of God!"
He sternly ordered them not to make Him known.
The Twelve
He went up the mountain and called to Him those He wanted, and they came to Him.
He appointed twelve, so that they might be with Him and that He might send them out to preach
and to have authority to drive out the demons.
He appointed the twelve: Simon, to whom He gave the name Peter;
James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, to whom He gave the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder;
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over.
Beelzebul
He went home, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
When His own people heard it, they went out to seize Him, for they were saying, "He is out of His mind."
The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the ruler of the demons He drives out the demons."
He called them to Him and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
If Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but his end has come.
No one can enter the strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first ties up the strong man; then he will plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, all things will be forgiven the sons of men, their sins and whatever blasphemies they utter;
but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin" —
for they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
His Mother and His Brothers
His mother and His brothers came, and standing outside they sent to Him and called Him.
A crowd was sitting around Him, and they said to Him, "Your mother and Your brothers are outside, looking for You."
He answered them, "Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?"
Looking around at those who sat in a circle around Him, He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers!
Whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother."

chapters.title: The Sower and the Storm
chapters.html:
Mark 4

The Sower

1Again He began to teach beside the sea. A very large crowd gathered around Him, so that He got into a boat on the sea and sat in it, and the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.

2He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said to them:

3"Listen! A sower went out to sow.

4As he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.

5Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up at once because the soil was not deep.

6When the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered.

7Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it bore no fruit.

8Other seeds fell into the good soil and bore fruit, coming up and growing, and they yielded thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold."

9He said, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."

Why Parables

10When He was alone, those around Him with the twelve asked Him about the parables.

11He said to them, "To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given; but for those outside everything comes in parables,

12so that 'they may look and look, and not see; and listen and listen, and not understand; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.'"

13He said to them, "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?

14The sower sows the word.

15These are the ones along the path where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan comes at once and takes away the word that was sown in them.

16In the same way, these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they at once receive it with joy;

17yet they have no root in themselves but last only a while; then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, at once they fall away.

18Others are the ones sown among the thorns: these are the ones who have heard the word,

19but the worries of this age, the deceitfulness of wealth and the desires for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

20Those sown on the good soil are the ones who hear the word and welcome it, and bear fruit, thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold."

A Lamp and a Measure

21He said to them, "Is a lamp brought in to be put under a basket, or under a bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?

22For nothing is hidden except to be made known, nor is anything secret except to be brought into the light.

23If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."

24He said to them, "Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.

25For whoever has, more will be given to him; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him."

Seeds Growing

26He said, "The kingdom of God is like this: a man scatters seed on the ground,

27and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, he does not know how.

28The earth bears fruit by itself: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain in the head.

29When the grain is ready, at once he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come."

30He said, "To what shall we compare the kingdom of God, or what parable shall we use for it?

31It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown on the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on the ground;

32yet when it is sown it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants, and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade."

33With many such parables He spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.

34He did not speak to them without a parable; but in private He explained everything to His own disciples.

The Storm

35That day, when evening came, He said to them, "Let us go across to the other side."

36Leaving the crowd, they took Him with them in the boat, just as He was; and other boats were with Him.

37A great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.

38He was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke Him and said to Him, "Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?"

39He woke up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, "Be quiet! Be still!" The wind stopped, and there was a great calm.

40He said to them, "Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?"

41They were filled with great fear and said to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?"

Notes

  • vv3–9 "Listen! A sower went out to sow… thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold" — Akouete, Listen!, opens the parable, and let him hear closes it (v9): it is a parable about hearing. Idou, look, after it is cut. Mark counts up, thirty, sixty, a hundred; Matthew counts down (Matthew 13:8).

  • vv10–12 "the mystery of the kingdom of God… they may look and look, and not see… otherwise they might turn and be forgiven" — mystērion, mystery, a secret now told to some; Matthew has mysteries (Matthew 13:11). The words are Isaiah's commission, otherwise they might see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn and be healed (Isaiah 6:10), in a short form that ends be forgiven. Hina, so that, gives the purpose, as in Isaiah, where the prophet is sent to make the heart fat.

  • vv13–20 "The sower sows the word… Satan comes at once and takes away the word" — ho logos, the word, eight times in the explanation: the seed is the message (2:2). Satan where Matthew has the evil one (Matthew 13:19). Skandalizontai, they fall away, word for word they are tripped up.

  • vv21–25 "Is a lamp brought in… With the measure you use… whoever has, more will be given" — erchetai ho lychnos, word for word does the lamp come, as if the lamp were a person arriving. The sayings stand apart in Matthew (Matthew 5:15; 7:2; 13:12); Mark sets them together after the sower. Blepete ti akouete, Pay attention to what you hear: the measure is how one listens.

  • vv26–29 "he does not know how… the earth bears fruit by itself… at once he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come" — only Mark has this parable. Automatē, by itself, the Greek word behind automatic. The last words are Joel's, Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe (Joel 3:13).

  • vv30–32 "a mustard seed… the birds of the sky can nest in its shade" — the great tree of the prophets, in the shade of its branches they will live (Ezekiel 17:23), and Nebuchadnezzar's tree, the birds of the heavens lived in its branches (Daniel 4:12): the smallest seed becomes the shelter of the nations. Matthew has becomes a tree (Matthew 13:32); Mark says larger than all the garden plants.

  • vv35–41 "asleep on the cushion… Be quiet! Be still!… Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" — Jonah too was asleep in the storm (Jonah 1:5). Pephimōso, Be still, is the verb of 1:25, Be silent: He speaks to the sea as to an unclean spirit. The psalms give this power to God, You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, You still them (Psalm 89:9), and He made the storm a whisper (Psalm 107:29). Ephobēthēsan phobon megan, filled with great fear, word for word feared a great fear: the calm frightens them more than the storm.

chapters.title: Legion, and Jairus's Daughter
chapters.html:
Mark 5

A Man Called Legion

1They came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gerasenes.

2When He had stepped out of the boat, at once a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet Him.

3He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him any longer, not even with a chain;

4for he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he had torn the chains apart and broken the shackles in pieces, and no one was strong enough to subdue him.

5Night and day, among the tombs and on the mountains, he was always crying out and cutting himself with stones.

6When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before Him,

7and crying out with a loud voice he said, "What have You to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I put You under oath by God: do not torment me!"

8For He had been saying to him, "Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!"

9He asked him, "What is your name?" He said to Him, "My name is Legion, for we are many."

10He begged Him earnestly not to send them out of the country.

11A great herd of pigs was feeding there on the mountainside,

12and they begged Him, "Send us into the pigs, so that we may go into them."

13He gave them leave. The unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd, about two thousand, rushed down the steep bank into the sea and were drowned in the sea.

14Those who tended them fled and told it in the town and in the countryside, and people came to see what had happened.

15They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by demons, the one who had had the legion, sitting there clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

16Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the man possessed by demons, and about the pigs.

17They began to beg Him to leave their region.

18As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons begged Him that he might be with Him.

19He did not let him, but said to him, "Go home to your own people, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how He has had mercy on you."

20He went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.

A Woman Who Touched His Cloak

21When Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered around Him; and He was beside the sea.

22One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and when he saw Him he fell at His feet

23and begged Him earnestly, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay Your hands on her, so that she may be made well and live."

24He went with him. A great crowd followed Him and pressed around Him.

25There was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,

26who had suffered much under many doctors and had spent all that she had, and was no better but rather grew worse.

27She had heard about Jesus, and she came up behind Him in the crowd and touched His cloak;

28for she said, "If I touch even His clothes, I will be made well."

29At once the source of her bleeding dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

30At once Jesus, knowing in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and said, "Who touched My clothes?"

31His disciples said to Him, "You see the crowd pressing around You, and You say, 'Who touched Me?'"

32He looked around to see who had done it.

33The woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him and told Him the whole truth.

34He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be healed of your affliction."

Talitha Koum

35While He was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader's house and said, "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any further?"

36But Jesus, overhearing what was said, said to the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid; only believe."

37He let no one follow Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

38They came to the synagogue leader's house, and He saw an uproar, people weeping and wailing loudly.

39He went in and said to them, "Why are you making an uproar and weeping? The child is not dead but asleep."

40They laughed at Him. But He put them all out, took the child's father and mother and those who were with Him, and went in where the child was.

41Taking the child by the hand, He said to her, "Talitha koum," which means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up."

42At once the girl got up and began to walk, for she was twelve years old. At once they were overcome with amazement.

43He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and told them to give her something to eat.

Notes

  • vv1–5 "the country of the Gerasenes… He lived among the tombs… cutting himself with stones" — Gerasēnōn, of the Gerasenes; Matthew has Gadarenes (Matthew 8:28). The other side of the sea is Gentile country, where pigs are kept. Tombs made a person unclean, whoever touches… a grave (Numbers 19:16), and Isaiah names among the rebellious those who sit among the graves… who eat the flesh of pigs (Isaiah 65:4). Matthew has two men; Mark tells of one.

  • vv6–7 "bowed down before Him… Son of the Most High God… I put You under oath by God" — prosekynēsen, bowed down, the word for worship. Tou hypsistou, the Most High, the name of God among the nations, as Melchizedek was a priest to God Most High (Genesis 14:18). Horkizō se, I put You under oath, the words the high priest uses to Jesus in Matthew 26:63.

  • vv9–13 "My name is Legion, for we are many… about two thousand" — legiōn, Legion, a soldiers' word, as in twelve legions of angels (Matthew 26:53). Epetrepsen, gave them leave.

  • vv15–20 "sitting there clothed and in his right mind… how much the Lord has done for you… how much Jesus had done for him" — the man once out of his mind is sōphronounta, in his right mind, while His own family thought Jesus out of His mind (3:21). Jesus sends him to tell what the Lord has done, and he tells what Jesus has done (vv19–20). Unlike the leper (1:44), he is told to speak: this is Gentile country. The Decapolis, the Ten Towns.

  • vv21–24 "One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus… My little daughter is at the point of death" — archisynagōgos, synagogue leader; Matthew calls him a leader (Matthew 9:18). In Matthew the daughter has just died; in Mark she is dying, and the news of her death comes in v35.

  • vv25–34 "a flow of blood for twelve years… If I touch even His clothes… Daughter, your faith has made you well" — the law made such a woman unclean all the days of her unclean flow (Leviticus 15:25), and what she touched unclean; her touch makes her clean. Sesōken se, has made you well, word for word has saved you, the same verb as v28. Mastix, affliction, word for word whip, as in 3:10. Twelve years she was sick, and the girl is twelve years old (v42): Mark sets the two stories one inside the other.

  • vv35–43 "Do not be afraid; only believe… Talitha koum… give her something to eat" — Talitha koum is Aramaic, and Mark gives its meaning, as with Boanerges (3:17). Elijah raised a child in a closed room, he stretched himself out on the child three times (1 Kings 17:21); here a word and a hand are enough. Exestēsan ekstasei megalē, word for word they were beside themselves with great astonishment. The food shows she is truly alive.

chapters.title: Five Loaves and Two Fish
chapters.html:
Mark 6

A Prophet Without Honor

1He went away from there and came to His home town, and His disciples followed Him.

2When the sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished, saying, "Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom given to Him, and these mighty works done by His hands?

3Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and the brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? Are not His sisters here with us?" They took offense at Him.

4Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his home town, among his relatives and in his own house."

5He could do no mighty work there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them.

6He was amazed at their unbelief. Then He went around the villages, teaching.

The Twelve Sent Out

7He called the twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.

8He commanded them to take nothing for the road except a staff: no bread, no bag, no copper in their belts;

9but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.

10He said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.

11If any place will not welcome you or listen to you, as you leave, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony to them."

12They went out and preached that people should repent.

13They drove out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

The Death of John

14King Herod heard of it, for His name had become known. People were saying, "John the baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him."

15Others said, "It is Elijah." Others said, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets."

16When Herod heard it, he said, "John, whom I beheaded, has been raised."

17For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison, because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, whom he had married.

18For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."

19Herodias held it against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not;

20for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. When he heard him he was greatly perplexed, and yet he liked to listen to him.

21An opportunity came when Herod on his birthday gave a banquet for his officials, the commanders and the leading men of Galilee.

22When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining at table with him. The king said to the girl, "Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you."

23He swore to her, "Whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."

24She went out and said to her mother, "What shall I ask for?" She said, "The head of John the baptizer."

25At once she hurried back to the king and asked, saying, "I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist."

26The king was deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those reclining at table, he did not want to refuse her.

27At once the king sent an executioner with orders to bring his head. He went and beheaded him in the prison,

28brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.

29When his disciples heard of it, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.

Five Thousand Fed

30The apostles gathered around Jesus and told Him all that they had done and taught.

31He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while." For many were coming and going, and they had no time even to eat.

32They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.

33Many saw them going and recognized them, and they ran there on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.

34When He went ashore, He saw a great crowd, and He was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep that have no shepherd; and He began to teach them many things.

35When it was already late, His disciples came to Him and said, "This is a deserted place, and the hour is already late.

36Send them away so that they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."

37He answered them, "You give them something to eat." They said to Him, "Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?"

38He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." When they had found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."

39He ordered them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.

40They sat down in companies, by hundreds and by fifties.

41Taking the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, said the blessing, broke the loaves and gave them to His disciples to set before the people; and He divided the two fish among them all.

42They all ate and were satisfied.

43They picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and of the fish.

44Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.

Walking on the Sea

45At once He made His disciples get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, to Bethsaida, while He sent the crowd away.

46After He had said goodbye to them, He went away to the mountain to pray.

47When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.

48He saw them straining at the oars, for the wind was against them. In the fourth watch of the night He came toward them, walking on the sea; and He meant to pass by them.

49When they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and cried out;

50for they all saw Him and were terrified. At once He spoke with them and said to them, "Take heart; I am the One. Do not be afraid."

51He got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were utterly astounded,

52for they had not understood about the loaves; their hearts were hardened.

53When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and moored there.

54When they got out of the boat, at once the people recognized Him,

55ran about that whole region, and began to carry the sick on their mats to wherever they heard He was.

56Wherever He went, into villages or towns or countryside, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him that they might touch even the tassel of His cloak; and all who touched it were made well.

Notes

  • vv1–6 "the carpenter, the son of Mary… they took offense at Him… He was amazed at their unbelief" — ho tektōn, the carpenter; Matthew has the carpenter's son (Matthew 13:55). The son of Mary, with no father named. Eskandalizonto, they took offense, the verb of 4:17. Ouk edynato, He could do no: Mark says could not, where Matthew says did not do many (Matthew 13:58). The brothers' names are as Matthew has them, with Joses for Joseph.

  • vv7–13 "two by two… nothing for the road except a staff… shake off the dust… anointed many sick people with oil" — in Matthew the twelve are told to take no sandals, no staff (Matthew 10:10); Mark allows both. Eis martyrion autois, as a testimony to them, the words of 1:44. Only Mark has the anointing with oil.

  • vv14–16 "King Herod… John… has been raised from the dead… Elijah… a prophet" — Matthew calls him Herod the tetrarch (Matthew 14:1); Mark gives him the title king, used five times in the story. The three guesses come back at 8:28. Ēgerthē, has been raised, the word of resurrection.

  • vv17–20 "the wife of his brother Philip… It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife… a righteous and holy man" — the law, You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife (Leviticus 18:16). Eneichen, held it against him, a grudge kept. Only Mark tells that Herod protected John and liked to listen to him.

  • vv21–29 "on his birthday gave a banquet… up to half of my kingdom… on a platter" — heōs hēmisous tēs basileias mou, up to half of my kingdom, as the Persian king promised Esther, Even to half of the kingdom, it shall be given you (Esther 5:3). Spekoulatōra, an executioner, a word borrowed from Latin. Ptōma, body, a corpse. The mother names him the baptizer (v24), the girl the Baptist (v25), Mark's two words.

  • vv30–44 "like sheep that have no shepherd… in groups on the green grass… by hundreds and by fifties… twelve baskets full" — the words Moses used when he asked for a leader, so that the congregation of the LORD may not be like sheep that have no shepherd (Numbers 27:17). The people are set out as Israel was in the wilderness, officers of hundreds, officers of fifties (Exodus 18:21). Symposia symposia… prasiai prasiai, word for word dinner party by dinner party… garden bed by garden bed, the crowd laid out in rows of color on the green. Elisha fed a hundred men with twenty loaves, they ate and had some left (2 Kings 4:44). A denarius was a day's wage (Matthew 20:2).

  • vv45–52 "walking on the sea… He meant to pass by them… Take heart; I am the One… their hearts were hardened" — Job says of God, He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the back of the sea (Job 9:8), and If He passes by me, I do not see Him (Job 9:11). Parelthein, to pass by, is the word of the LORD's glory before Moses, when My glory passes by (Exodus 33:22). Egō eimi, I am the One, as Matthew 14:27, the words that can mean It is I and recall the name of God (Exodus 3:14). Pepōrōmenē, hardened, from the root of the hardness of their hearts in 3:5, now said of the disciples.

speech.text: Mark 6
A Prophet Without Honor
He went away from there and came to His home town, and His disciples followed Him.

When the sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished, saying, "Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom given to Him, and these mighty works done by His hands?
Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and the brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? Are not His sisters here with us?" They took offense at Him.
Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his home town, among his relatives and in his own house."
He could do no mighty work there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He was amazed at their unbelief. Then He went around the villages, teaching.
The Twelve Sent Out
He called the twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
He commanded them to take nothing for the road except a staff: no bread, no bag, no copper in their belts;
but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.
He said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.
If any place will not welcome you or listen to you, as you leave, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony to them."
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They drove out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
The Death of John
King Herod heard of it, for His name had become known. People were saying, "John the baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him."
Others said, "It is Elijah." Others said, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets."
When Herod heard it, he said, "John, whom I beheaded, has been raised."
For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison, because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, whom he had married.
For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
Herodias held it against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not;
for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. When he heard him he was greatly perplexed, and yet he liked to listen to him.
An opportunity came when Herod on his birthday gave a banquet for his officials, the commanders and the leading men of Galilee.

When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining at table with him. The king said to the girl, "Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you."
He swore to her, "Whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."
She went out and said to her mother, "What shall I ask for?" She said, "The head of John the baptizer."
At once she hurried back to the king and asked, saying, "I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
The king was deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those reclining at table, he did not want to refuse her.
At once the king sent an executioner with orders to bring his head. He went and beheaded him in the prison,
brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
When his disciples heard of it, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.
Five Thousand Fed
The apostles gathered around Jesus and told Him all that they had done and taught.
He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while." For many were coming and going, and they had no time even to eat.
They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
Many saw them going and recognized them, and they ran there on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.
When He went ashore, He saw a great crowd, and He was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep that have no shepherd; and He began to teach them many things.
When it was already late, His disciples came to Him and said, "This is a deserted place, and the hour is already late.
Send them away so that they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
He answered them, "You give them something to eat." They said to Him, "Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?"
He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." When they had found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."
He ordered them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in companies, by hundreds and by fifties.

Taking the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, said the blessing, broke the loaves and gave them to His disciples to set before the people; and He divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
They picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and of the fish.
Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
Walking on the Sea
At once He made His disciples get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, to Bethsaida, while He sent the crowd away.
After He had said goodbye to them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.
He saw them straining at the oars, for the wind was against them. In the fourth watch of the night He came toward them, walking on the sea; and He meant to pass by them.
When they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and cried out;
for they all saw Him and were terrified. At once He spoke with them and said to them, "Take heart; I am the One. Do not be afraid."
He got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were utterly astounded,
for they had not understood about the loaves; their hearts were hardened.
When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and moored there.
When they got out of the boat, at once the people recognized Him,
ran about that whole region, and began to carry the sick on their mats to wherever they heard He was.

Wherever He went, into villages or towns or countryside, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him that they might touch even the tassel of His cloak; and all who touched it were made well.
